newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Jan 27-31 program trading averaged 13.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Jan 27-31 program trading averaged 13.2 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading averaged 13.2 percent of its average daily volume of 517.3 million shares, or 68.1 million shares a day, from January 27 to January 31.
Of the average, buy programs accounted for an average of 31.4 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average of 36.7 milion daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 103.5 million shares during the week.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities executed all of its program activity for customers, as agent. Salomon Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Nomura Securities and First Boston executed most of their program activity as principal, for their own accounts.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 61.3 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 38.1 percent of program volume.
Between January 27 and 31, 23.5 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while another 0.9 percent involved derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
